title: The Standard Production Stack
objectives: Know the default production packages and their purpose
Recognize when each is NOT needed
Prefer maintained, focused packages over kitchen sinks

examples.name: stack.txt
examples.code:
helmet             -> security headers          (skip: pure HTML site behind a proxy that sets headers)
pino               -> structured logging        (skip: tiny internal script)
express-rate-limit -> brute-force protection    (skip: only behind a gateway that rate limits)
zod / joi          -> schema validation         (skip: one endpoint, plain manual checks)
dotenv-style env   -> local env loading         (skip: platform injects env already)

NOT defaults: ORM (choose deliberately), test framework (node:test may suffice),
utility belts (lodash — most uses are native now)

exercise.prompt: Match package to purpose: "helmet" (security headers), "pino" (structured logs), "express-rate-limit" (brute force), "zod" (schema validation).
hints: Each default package maps to a named attack/need.
If nothing needs the protection, the package is weight.

questions.prompt: The justification test for each default package is…
options: which attack or need does it address, and is anything already doing that
questions.explanation: Packages earn their place per named risk — and lose it when a proxy/gateway already covers it.

questions.prompt: A kitchen-sink utility library today is usually…
options: mostly replaceable by native JS (fetch, structuredClone, array methods)
questions.explanation: Native JS absorbed most lodash use-cases; import only what is genuinely missing.
